answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with quadratic endorsement cost. Each agent's endorsements of a newcomer cost stake that grows quadratically with the number of identities it vouches for, so spawning a nebula of fake accounts drains the attacker's own treasury fast. A newcomer starts at its nadir: zero trust, tiny rate limits, and no voting weight, and it must earn standing by completing verified useful work in the open meadow of public tasks before any endorsement unlocks real privileges. Creating one honest identity stays cheap; manufacturing a thousand becomes ruinously expensive.
